title: The Training Characteristics of World-Class Distance Runners: An Integration of Scientific Literature and Results-Proven Practice
authors: Haugen T, Sandbakk O, Seiler S, Tonnessen E
population: World-class 5000/10,000 m and marathon runners (literature plus coaching practice)
findings: Mid-preparation weekly distance is 160-220 km for marathoners and 130-190 km for track runners; both groups perform 11-14 sessions per week.
At least 80% of total running volume is performed at low intensity throughout the training year.
TID varies across mesocycles and differs between marathon and track runners, but volume of race-pace running increases as the main competition approaches.
Tapering starts 7-10 days before the main competition.
limitations: Narrative integration for world-class runners; volumes and frequencies do not transfer to recreational athletes; no controlled comparison.
implications: Use >=80% low-intensity volume as the annual floor, scaled to the athlete's own load rather than elite absolute volume.
Increase the race-pace share as the goal race approaches.
Taper timing belongs to the taper topic; 7-10 days is an elite figure and needs scaling for lower-volume athletes.

verification.notes: Crossref: online 2022-04-01, journal matches. All figures from abstract.
